title: It was founded in 1889, making playing cards.
description:
It was founded in 1889, making playing cards. Hand-painted hanafuda (Japanese flower cards) crafted from mulberry bark in a Kyoto workshop. It is still headquartered in Kyoto today.

He opened the shop as Nintendo Koppai. By 1929 it was the largest card maker in Japan, and in 1959 a deal with Disney put Mickey Mouse on the decks: a record 600,000 sold that year.

From that first deck of flower cards to the Game Boy of 1989, a full century before Nintendo's most famous handheld.

In the 1960s it ran a taxi firm and sold instant rice. Flush from going public, Nintendo sold packets of instant rice (a flop), ran the Daiya taxi company, and even opened an hourly-rental hotel, before deciding toys and games were its future.

For its first eighty years, the maker of Mario never sold a single video game.

Sources:
- https://www.britannica.com/money/Nintendo-Company-Ltd: Encyclopaedia Britannica, read in full (fact-checked). Establishes: Nintendo was founded in 1889 by Yamauchi Fusajiro as Nintendo Koppai, making handmade hanafuda playing cards, and has been headquartered in Kyoto since; in the early 1900s it became the first Japanese company to make Western-style cards (crafted from mulberry bark); it was the largest playing-card maker in Japan by 1929; a 1959 Disney licensing deal sold a record 600,000 decks; after going public in the early 1960s it funded failed ventures (individually packaged instant rice, a 'love hotel' with hourly room rentals, and the Daiya taxi company) before establishing a games department in 1969; Gunpei Yokoi's Ultra Hand (about 1970) sold over a million units; and the Game Boy launched in 1989.
- https://www.cbr.com/nintendo-different-company-video-games/: CBR (Zack Millsap, 24 Nov 2020), read in full. Corroborates the 1889 hanafuda origin under Fusajiro Yamauchi, the 1959 Disney deal, and the 1960s diversification under Hiroshi Yamauchi into instant rice, love hotels, and the Daiya taxi service, followed by the pivot to toys (Gunpei Yokoi) and the 1977 Color TV-Game consoles.
